item.title: Veterans Crisis Line: Actions Needed to Improve Services Provided After Initial Contact
item.description:
What GAO Found
Suicide prevention is the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) stated top clinical priority. To this end, VA operates the Veterans Crisis Line (VCL), a 24/7 phone, chat, and text service. The VCL is staffed by crisis responders who support veterans and their family and friends (VA refers to users of the VCL as customers). VA offers a variety of immediate and long-term post-contact services to customers following their crisis line interactions, such as peer support and requests for follow-up from suicide prevention coordinators at local VA medical facilities.
Process for Delivering Services Following Veterans Crisis Line Interactions
VCL officials and staff at six medical facilities GAO reviewed reported challenges coordinating emergency crisis interventions. In particular, according to VCL officials, some jurisdictions will not dispatch emergency responders to VCL customers due to local challenges, such as low law enforcement availability. GAO found that VCL does not proactively identify other local emergency response resources with which the VCL could coordinate emergency responses in these jurisdictions, such as mobile crisis units. Rather, VA policy calls for VCL employees to research potential local resources in real-time. Having information on alternative resources readily available would help ensure the VCL’s ability to respond in a timely manner to emergencies.
To evaluate the effectiveness of VCL post-contact services, VA researchers have conducted studies on some of these services, such as emergency crisis services and caring letters. VA also collects information on post-contact services provided after a VCL call. For instance, VA tracks whether suicide prevention coordinators at VA medical facilities attempt to contact veterans to discuss requests for follow up care at VA, as required by VA policy. However, VA does not collect and track VCL request data on the extent to which (1) the coordinators are successfully reaching veterans and (2) veterans are connecting to care in accordance with each veteran’s needs and preferences. Collecting and tracking such information would provide evidence VA could use to assess its process for following up with veterans after their interactions with the VCL and to better ensure the department is supporting veterans and meeting their needs and preferences.
Why GAO Did This Study
Suicide is one of the leading causes of death in the United States and veterans suffer a disproportionately high rate of suicide compared to non-veterans. Use of the VCL has grown over the last several years, with over 1.2 million interactions in fiscal year 2025. VCL crisis responders handle initial communications with individuals and can refer customers to post-VCL contact services.
GAO was asked to review aspects of VCL post-contact services. This report (1) describes post-contact services; (2) examines challenges associated with providing post-contact services; and (3) examines the extent to which VA has evaluated the effectiveness of its post-VCL contact services.
GAO reviewed VA policies, interviewed VA officials, analyzed fiscal year 2021-2025 data on post-contact services, conducted site visits at six medical facilities selected based on complexity and geographic variation, and reviewed a non-generalized sample of medical records.
